title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Sensor Refill Shipment: Representative System Reference Card
content:
Representative system reference card — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, Larkfield Medical Supply.

## Where this card applies

Larkfield's Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program has a rule that counts the billing units of a sensor refill (A4239) on a tier where each refill requires the customer's own confirmation — the CGM Commercial HMO Program, CGM Commercial PPO Program, CGM Medicare Advantage Program, CGM Original Medicare Program and CGM Medicaid Program — when the refill the customer asks for draws on the authorization grant resting on the newest written order of the item. The rule governs how many billing units that refill ships; the shipment is booked with `ship_sensor_refill_e9d57917`.

## Rule clauses

1. A refill draws no units until the newest written order of the item stands recorded as an authorization grant resting on that order.
2. A refill does not ship until the program's past-due amount, once the balance an approved payment plan on the program covers is left out, is below the tier's past-due hold minimum.
3. Confirmation. For a refill this rule counts, the customer confirms in the call in which they ask for it that they are still using the item and how much supply they have on hand, and that confirmation is recorded as the shipment's refill confirmation date, the ship date; every other refill on tiers where each refill requires the customer's own confirmation ships only after the customer personally confirms, for that shipment, that they are still using the item and how much supply they have on hand, with the confirmation date recorded on the shipment; Larkfield never ships those tiers automatically, and Larkfield's own refill reminder for those tiers is made no sooner than the tier's refill reminder lead time before the planned ship date.
4. Days of supply. For a refill this rule counts, and only for such a refill, the supply days of the shipment are 30 days for each billing unit that ships under this rule at the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply, out of the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment shortened to the whole 30-day blocks that remain before the authorization's valid-through date when fewer remain; for every other refill the supply days of a shipment are the tier's standard days of supply per refill shipment, shortened to the whole 30-day blocks that remain before the authorization's valid-through date when fewer remain.

Clause 1 in other words: until a grant resting on the newest written order of the item is on record, the refill draws no units at all. Clause 2 in other words: while the past-due amount, with the plan-covered balance left out, is at or above the tier's past-due hold minimum, the refill does not ship.

## The tool: `ship_sensor_refill_e9d57917`

Capability. The tool ships one CGM sensor refill package on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program enrollment: Larkfield records one refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance (A4239), shipped today by standard ground and billed by payer claim, drawing the stated billing units on the stated authorization grant; it records today's date as the customer's refill confirmation, and debits the units from the enrollment's units still authorized to ship. Afterwards the enrollment's shipment history shows the new package with its units, sensor count and days of supply, and its units still authorized to ship fall by the units shipped.

How it is invoked. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `ship_sensor_refill_e9d57917` and then calls it with the parameters below.

Parameters.

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `cgm_program_id` | the reference number of the CGM supply program enrollment the refill ships on, as returned by the CGM program lookup | identifier |
| `cgm_order_id` | the reference number of the authorization grant the refill draws on, as returned by the CGM prescription and authorization file lookup or by the tool that recorded the authorization | identifier |
| `previous_cgm_shipment_id` | the reference number of the enrollment's latest earlier refill shipment of the item, as returned by the CGM shipment history lookup | identifier |
| `coverage_id` | the reference number of the coverage record the enrollment bills, as returned by the coverage lookup | identifier |
| `customer_id` | the reference number of the customer profile, as returned by the customer lookup | identifier |
| `units` | the billing units shipped | a positive integer in billing units, no decimals |
| `pieces` | the physical sensors in the package | an integer count of physical pieces, no decimals |
| `supply_days` | the days of supply the package covers | an integer number of calendar days, a multiple of 30, no decimals |

No parameter takes a fixed list of values.

Return. On success the tool returns a confirmation sentence naming the new shipment's reference number (the prefix `ship_` followed by 12 hexadecimal characters), the enrollment reference number, the units, pieces and days of supply shipped, the ship date in YYYY-MM-DD format, and the enrollment's units still authorized to ship after the debit, as a whole number. The presence of the shipment reference number shows that the refill was shipped and recorded. The tool defines no other return.

## Reference questions

- Which date becomes the refill confirmation date of a refill this rule counts? The ship date: the tool records today's date both as the ship date and as the customer's refill confirmation.
- Shape of a call's receipt (format placeholders only): a call with `units` of <units>, `pieces` of <pieces> and `supply_days` of <days> returns a sentence naming a shipment reference `ship_<12 hexadecimal characters>`, <units> unit(s), <pieces> sensor(s), <days> days of supply, today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format, and the enrollment's units still authorized to ship after the <units> unit(s) are debited.
